correctness.rationale: The claim is for the two presented groups of order 4n, not every group with an index-two cyclic subgroup. In each, the cyclic subgroup of order 2n has inversion as the action of the other coset. A character of that subgroup of order d>2 is not fixed by inversion, and induction gives a degree-two irreducible; different pairs {λ,λ⁻¹} are inequivalent by restriction. The induced character is zero off the subgroup and restricts to λ+λ⁻¹, so its kernel is ker λ and its codegree is d. There are φ(d)/2 inversion pairs of exact order d. The abelianization is C₂×C₂ in the dihedral case and in the even dicyclic case; for odd n it is C₄ by a=x². The principal and three other linear characters exhaust the missing degree squares, since 4+4(n−1)=4n. Linear codegree equals image order, yielding the stated additions; 4 does not divide 2n for odd n and does not merge. The criterion follows, and n=2 gives the stated Q₈/D₈ multiplicities. For all n≥2, an element off the dicyclic rotation subgroup squares to aⁿ≠1, whereas every element in the dihedral reflection coset squares to 1; the involution counts differ. The packaged artifacts/verify.py was inspected, not executed. Its finite checks are not needed for the proof.

value.rationale: The exact parity criterion tests a structural question about an invariant intended to distinguish finite groups: it determines precisely when it cannot see the distinction between the two canonical inversion extensions with the same order, producing nonisomorphic collisions beyond 2-groups and a uniform contrasting odd branch.
